title: Viva Engage: community feeds default to all posts, sorted by recent posts
summary: The briefing passes: its default, feed behaviour, scope and rollout window agree with Microsoft's records. Licensing should identify the published Viva Engage Core entitlement rather than leave the model unknown, and the rollout checklist should describe November completion as expected, not guaranteed.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Community feeds will default to all posts.
claims.quote: Communities will default to “all” and “recent posts”:

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Community feeds will default to sorting by recent posts rather than recent activity.
claims.quote: We’re introducing a simpler way to view conversations in Viva Engage communities, organized by recent posts rather than recent activity.

claims.claim: The current experience defaults to the new feed when there are new posts or replies.
claims.quote: Communities default to “new” and “recent activity” if there’s any new content (posts or replies).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The current default sort is recent activity when new content exists.
claims.quote: Communities default to “new” and “recent activity” if there’s any new content (posts or replies).

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The current feed falls back to all when there is no new content.
claims.quote: If there’s no new content, the feed falls back to “all.”

claims.claim: Current unread indicators exist only in the new feed.
claims.quote: Unread indicators on content only exist in the “new” feed.

claims.claim: The new experience will show unread indicators in both the new and all feeds.
claims.quote: Unread indicators will exist in both the “new” and “all” feeds.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A user's choice of new or all will be maintained across communities.
claims.quote: If someone changes the feed (new/all) or sort order (recent posts/recent activity), we will maintain that setting across their communities.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: A user's choice of recent posts or recent activity will be maintained across communities.
claims.quote: If someone changes the feed (new/all) or sort order (recent posts/recent activity), we will maintain that setting across their communities.

claims.claim: A user who prefers new will see all for a visit to a community with no new content.
claims.quote: If someone picks “new” and there’s no new content in the next community, we will fall back to “all” for that community visit

claims.claim: Falling back to all for an empty-new-content visit does not erase the user's new preference.
claims.quote: but “new” will remain the preference for that user.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can still choose recent activity sorting and filtering to new conversations only.
claims.quote: will be available as an option, alongside the current system, for those who prefer sorting by recent activity and filtering to new conversations only.
